response.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT p.player_id, COUNT(ma.player_id) AS award_count FROM player p LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON ma.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id), totals AS (SELECT SUM(award_count) AS total_count FROM counts) SELECT c.player_id, c.award_count, c.award_count * 1.0 / NULLIF(t.total_count, 0) AS fraction FROM counts c CROSS JOIN totals t ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each player_id appears once in the player table, so each player yields one output row.
The number of manager_award records is the row count per player_id, so a player with no rows gets 0 through the LEFT JOIN and COUNT of the joined column.

The total is the sum of the per-player counts. A missing total (NULL, e.g. an empty player table) and a zero total (no manager awards at all) both produce a NULL fraction, since a zero total makes the fraction undefined.
Players tied on fraction are ordered arbitrarily, so which tied players appear at the 10-row cutoff is not determined by the request.
